title: Market-response simulation: pricing sensitivity for on-prem vs hosted inference in regulated SMBs
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective: Build a quantitative simulation and recommendation set to understand how SMB buyers in regulated verticals (finserv, healthcare, legal tech) trade off price, latency, and deployment mode (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/on-prem). The output will be: 1) a demand elasticity matrix by vertical and use-case; 2) recommended pricing levers and commitment thresholds for Dedicated and Private offerings; 3) a prioritized experiment plan for sales pilots and A/B pricing tests.

Background: We have qualitative signals that enterprise buyers value Private/Dedicated for compliance and predictability, but SMB buyers in regulated pockets are price-sensitive and use short-term bursts or hybrid patterns. Existing PM research has lots of model-supply data; we need a complementary demand-side model to inform packaging (reserve sizes, overage pricing, credit/seat bundles).

Hypotheses: 1) SMB buyers with moderate compliance needs will accept ~25-40% premium for private deployment only if latency and cost predictability are demonstrable. 2) Short-duration workloads (RAG retrievals, weekly batch scoring) are more price elastic than low-latency chat endpoints. 3) A small committed-capacity discount + predictable SLOs will move ~18-25% of SMB trials to Dedicated in the first year.

Approach:
- Data pulls: instrument usage cohorts (trial->paid conversion), per-customer token economics, latency buckets, geographic region. Query Looker/BigQuery slices and stylize as synthetic cohorts.
- Build a Monte Carlo-based demand simulator that varies price, latency SLOs, and commitment size to estimate conversion and revenue uplift.
- Calibrate simulator with three sources: (a) historical Redwood billing/usage data for SMBs, (b) sales win/loss notes for regulated accounts, (c) 12 customer interviews (sales-run) focused on procurement thresholds.
- Sensitivity analysis: run scenarios for 6, 12, 24-month commitments, burst vs continuous usage, and quantized latency guarantees (50ms/100ms/250ms).

Deliverables:
- Elasticity matrix CSV (vertical x use-case x deployment mode)
- Executive one-pager with recommended pricing tiers and margin impact projection
- Experiment plan (3x sales pilots + 2x staged pricing A/B tests)
- Notebook + reproducible simulation artifacts in GitHub

Assumptions:
- Cost per token throughput based on runtime-1.20 kernel cost curves (approx current estimates).
- Sales conversion lift estimates use conservative priors (Beta(2,8)).
- No major supply constraints for Dedicated within regional pools for pilot cohorts.

Stakeholders: Growth Sales (pilot leads), Revenue Ops (billing changes), Eng (cost model correctness), Legal (compliance claims), Finance (revenue projection sign-off).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Simulator runs reproducible scenarios and produces elasticity matrix CSV; 2) VP Sales and Finance sign off on recommended pricing levers; 3) Experiment plan has measurable primary metric (conversion delta) and instrumentation TODOs assigned; 4) Notebook and dataset assets uploaded to GH and GDrive with README.
